To prevent Sybil attacks in an autonomous AI economy, systems
 can implement computational proof-of-work tied to cryptographic memory graphs, functioning like a data river that continuously flows to verify historical compute. If an attacker tries to spin up multiple fraudulent instances to manipulate a governance thread, they face exorbitant costs. Generating valid cryptographic proofs requires massive GPU cycles and sustained electrical power, rendering the fake identities economically unviable and reducing the threat of exploitation to a mere fable.
